strengths: Title and H1 match informational intent: why orderly lines, not a manners listicle
Intro promises mechanism plus where it breaks—matches ‘is Japan really that polite in lines?’ curiosity
H2s are natural language (floor marks, local experience, myth, scenarios, tips, FAQ)
Keywords (queuing, platforms, waiting) appear in context without stuffing
Internal links to escalators, punctuality, and sumimasen support related intent without hijacking the page

issues.problem: Searchers often type ‘is it rude to cut in line in Japan’ / ‘Japan queue etiquette.’ Cutting is answered, but the heading is only ‘Do people ever cut?’
issues.suggestion: Optional: add rudeness to that answer in one clause. Do not keyword-stuff a new H2.

issues.problem: Classroom-cleaning is a mild off-intent digression for a queuing query.
issues.suggestion: Keep station/school-lining links; leave cleaning to its own article.
